products.name: cybersecurity_incident
products.description: Master record for every cybersecurity incident investigated by the institution's information security office, including phishing attacks, malware infections, unauthorized access, data breaches, ransomware events, and insider threats. Captures incident identifier, incident classification (per NIST CSF or institutional taxonomy), detection source (SIEM alert, user report, threat intel feed), affected systems and data types, data sensitivity level (FERPA, HIPAA, PCI, research data), containment actions taken, eradication steps, recovery actions, notification obligations triggered (FERPA breach, state breach notification law), regulatory reporting deadlines, incident severity, and lessons-learned summary. Distinct from the ITSM incident in that cybersecurity incidents involve security investigation workflows, legal/compliance notification, and forensic evidence handling.

attributes.name: cybersecurity_incident_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the cybersecurity incident record. Primary key for the cybersecurity incident entity.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 Computer Security Incident Handling Guide

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the information security staff member or incident response team member assigned as the primary investigator for this incident. Links to employee or user identity record.

attributes.name: identity_account_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user (student, faculty, staff) who initially reported the incident, if applicable. Links to user or employee identity record. Null if incident was detected by automated systems.

attributes.name: incident_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.incident. Business justification: Cybersecurity incidents often generate corresponding ITSM incident tickets for operational tracking and resolution. The related_itsm_incident_number STRING should normalize to incident_id FK. This lin

attributes.name: affected_data_types
attributes.description: Description of the categories of data potentially exposed, accessed, or compromised during the incident. Examples include student academic records, financial aid data, employee payroll information, research data, or health records.
attributes.references: FERPA 34 CFR Part 99, HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR Part 164

attributes.name: affected_systems
attributes.description: Comma-separated list or narrative description of institutional IT systems, applications, servers, or network segments impacted by the cybersecurity incident. May include Student Information System (SIS), Learning Management System (LMS), email servers, file shares, or research computing infrastructure.

attributes.name: assigned_investigator_name
attributes.description: Full name of the primary incident investigator for display and reporting purposes. Denormalized for operational convenience.

attributes.name: attack_vector
attributes.description: Description of the method or pathway used by the attacker to compromise systems or data. Examples include phishing email, unpatched vulnerability, stolen credentials, malicious attachment, drive-by download, or SQL injection.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2, MITRE ATT&CK Framework

attributes.name: closed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the incident was formally closed after all response activities, notifications, and documentation were completed. Marks the end of the incident lifecycle.

attributes.name: closure_notes
attributes.description: Final summary notes documenting the resolution of the incident, including confirmation of eradication, validation of recovery, completion of notifications, and any outstanding follow-up actions or monitoring requirements.

attributes.name: containment_actions
attributes.description: Narrative summary of immediate containment steps taken to limit the scope and impact of the incident. Actions may include isolating affected systems, disabling compromised accounts, blocking malicious IP addresses, or shutting down network segments.

attributes.name: containment_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the incident was successfully contained, preventing further unauthorized access or data exfiltration. Marks the transition from active threat to controlled investigation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this cybersecurity incident record was first created in the information security incident management system. Used for audit trail and record lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: data_sensitivity_level
attributes.description: Highest classification level of data involved in the incident, determining regulatory notification and breach response obligations. Categories include FERPA-protected education records, HIPAA Protected Health Information (PHI), Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) cardholder data, controlled research data, or public information.
attributes.references: FERPA 34 CFR 99.31, HIPAA 45 CFR 164.402, PCI DSS v4.0

attributes.name: detection_source
attributes.description: The channel or mechanism through which the incident was initially detected. Sources include Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) alerts, user reports, threat intelligence feeds, vulnerability scans, audit log reviews, or external notifications from partners or law enforcement.

attributes.name: detection_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the cybersecurity incident was first detected or reported, representing the initial awareness event. This is the principal business event timestamp for the incident lifecycle.

attributes.name: eradication_actions
attributes.description: Narrative summary of eradication steps taken to remove the threat from the environment. Actions may include malware removal, patching vulnerabilities, deleting unauthorized accounts, or rebuilding compromised systems.

attributes.name: eradication_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the threat was fully eradicated from institutional systems and the root cause was addressed. Marks completion of threat removal activities.

attributes.name: estimated_financial_impact
attributes.description: Estimated total financial cost of the incident in U.S. dollars, including investigation costs, remediation expenses, notification costs, legal fees, regulatory fines, and business disruption losses. Used for risk quantification and insurance claims.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2, NACUBO Financial Reporting Standards

attributes.name: estimated_record_count
attributes.description: Estimated number of individual records (student records, employee records, patient records, etc.) potentially affected by the incident. Used for breach notification threshold determination and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: FERPA Breach Notification Guidance, State Breach Notification Laws

attributes.name: forensic_evidence_collected_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether digital forensic evidence was collected and preserved during the incident investigation. True indicates evidence was collected for potential legal proceedings or detailed analysis; false indicates no forensic collection.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2, ISO/IEC 27037 Digital Evidence Guidelines

attributes.name: forensic_evidence_location
attributes.description: Secure storage location or reference identifier for collected forensic evidence, including disk images, memory dumps, log files, or network packet captures. Maintained for chain of custody and potential legal proceedings.

attributes.name: incident_classification
attributes.description: Primary classification of the cybersecurity incident type per institutional taxonomy aligned with NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF). Categories include phishing attacks, malware infections, unauthorized access attempts, data breaches, ransomware events, and insider threats.
attributes.references: NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF), NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2

attributes.name: incident_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the cybersecurity incident, including initial symptoms, observed behavior, affected users or systems, and preliminary assessment. Provides context for investigation and response activities.

attributes.name: incident_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the cybersecurity incident investigation and response workflow. Tracks progression from initial detection through containment, eradication, recovery, and closure.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 Incident Response Lifecycle

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this cybersecurity incident record was most recently updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking throughout the incident lifecycle.

attributes.name: law_enforcement_case_number
attributes.description: Case or reference number assigned by law enforcement agency if the incident was reported for criminal investigation. Used for coordination with law enforcement and tracking legal proceedings.

attributes.name: law_enforcement_notified_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether law enforcement agencies (FBI, Secret Service, state/local police) were notified of the incident. True indicates law enforcement involvement; false indicates no law enforcement notification.

attributes.name: lessons_learned_summary
attributes.description: Summary of key lessons learned from the incident response process, including what worked well, what could be improved, and recommendations for policy, process, or technology enhancements to prevent recurrence.

attributes.name: mitre_attack_techniques
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of MITRE ATT&CK technique identifiers (e.g., T1566.001 for Spearphishing Attachment) observed during the incident. Used for threat intelligence sharing and defensive control mapping.

attributes.name: notification_completed_date
attributes.description: Date when all required breach notifications were completed and documented. Used to demonstrate compliance with notification deadlines and regulatory requirements.
attributes.references: FERPA, HIPAA, State Breach Notification Laws

attributes.name: notification_deadline_date
attributes.description: Regulatory or legal deadline by which affected parties and agencies must be notified of the breach. Calculated based on applicable law (e.g., HIPAA requires notification within 60 days of discovery; state laws vary from immediate to 90 days).
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR 164.404, State Breach Notification Laws

attributes.name: notification_obligations
attributes.description: Description of specific notification requirements triggered by the incident, including affected parties (students, employees, patients), regulatory agencies (U.S. Department of Education, state attorneys general), and notification timelines. May reference FERPA breach notification, HIPAA breach notification, or state-specific breach laws.
attributes.references: FERPA 34 CFR 99.31, HIPAA 45 CFR 164.404-414, State Breach Notification Statutes

attributes.name: notification_required_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the incident triggers regulatory or legal notification obligations under FERPA breach notification requirements, state breach notification laws, or contractual obligations. True indicates notification is required; false indicates no notification obligation.
attributes.references: FERPA 34 CFR 99.31, State Breach Notification Laws

attributes.name: recovery_actions
attributes.description: Narrative summary of recovery steps taken to restore affected systems and services to normal operation. Actions may include restoring from backups, reconfiguring systems, validating data integrity, or re-enabling user access.

attributes.name: recovery_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when affected systems and services were fully restored to normal operation and validated for safe use. Marks the return to business-as-usual state.

attributes.name: reported_by_user_name
attributes.description: Full name of the user who reported the incident, if applicable. Denormalized for operational convenience and recognition purposes.

attributes.name: root_cause_analysis
attributes.description: Detailed narrative of the root cause investigation findings, identifying the underlying vulnerability, misconfiguration, or human error that enabled the incident. Used for lessons learned and preventive control implementation.

attributes.name: severity_level
attributes.description: Assessed severity of the cybersecurity incident based on impact to confidentiality, integrity, and availability of institutional systems and data. Critical incidents involve significant data breaches or system compromise; low incidents involve minor policy violations with no data exposure.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2, FERPA Security Rule

attributes.name: threat_actor_type
attributes.description: Classification of the suspected threat actor behind the incident based on tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs). Categories include nation-state actors, organized cybercrime groups, hacktivists, malicious insiders, opportunistic attackers, or unknown.

attributes.name: related_cybersecurity_incident_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on cybersecurity_incident (related_cybersecurity_incident_id)

products.name: vulnerability
products.description: Master record for every identified security vulnerability tracked by the institution's vulnerability management program, sourced from automated scanning tools (Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7), penetration testing engagements, and vendor security advisories (CVEs). Captures CVE identifier, CVSS base score, vulnerability title, affected asset or software, affected system count, discovery date, discovery source, remediation owner, remediation due date (based on severity SLA), remediation status (open, in-remediation, remediated, accepted-risk, false-positive), remediation action taken, and risk acceptance justification when applicable. Enables institutional vulnerability SLA compliance tracking and feeds cybersecurity risk reporting.

attributes.name: vulnerability_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the security vulnerability record in the institution's vulnerability management program.

attributes.name: configuration_item_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.configuration_item. Business justification: Vulnerabilities are discovered on specific configuration items (servers, network devices, applications). The affected_asset_identifier STRING should normalize to configuration_item_id FK. This links v

attributes.name: affected_software_name
attributes.description: Name of the software product, operating system, or application component that contains the vulnerability.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: affected_software_vendor
attributes.description: Name of the software vendor or publisher that produces the affected software product.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: affected_software_version
attributes.description: Version number or build identifier of the affected software product in which the vulnerability exists.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: affected_system_count
attributes.description: Total number of institutional systems, devices, or application instances affected by this vulnerability, used to assess institutional exposure and prioritize remediation efforts.

attributes.name: business_criticality
attributes.description: Business criticality rating of the affected system or application (mission-critical, high, medium, low), used to prioritize remediation based on operational impact.

attributes.name: compliance_framework_impact
attributes.description: Identification of regulatory or compliance frameworks (FERPA, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, FISMA, state data breach laws) that may be impacted by this vulnerability if exploited, used to prioritize remediation for compliance-critical systems.
attributes.references: FERPA 34 CFR Part 99, HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.308, PCI-DSS Requirement 6

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this vulnerability record was first created in the vulnerability management system.

attributes.name: cve_identifier
attributes.description: Standardized CVE identifier assigned by MITRE for publicly disclosed vulnerabilities, enabling cross-reference with national vulnerability databases and vendor advisories.
attributes.references: NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD), MITRE CVE Program

attributes.name: cvss_base_score
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) Base Score
attributes.description: Numeric severity score (0.0 to 10.0) calculated using the CVSS framework, representing the intrinsic characteristics of the vulnerability independent of temporal or environmental factors.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-126 Technical Specification for CVSS, FIRST CVSS v3.1

attributes.name: cvss_vector_string
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) Vector String
attributes.description: Compressed textual representation of the CVSS metric values (e.g., CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H) used to derive the base score.

attributes.name: data_classification_exposure
attributes.description: Highest data classification level of information that could be exposed if this vulnerability is exploited, used to assess business impact and prioritize remediation.

attributes.name: discovery_date
attributes.description: Date on which the vulnerability was first identified within the institution's environment through automated scanning, penetration testing, or vendor advisory.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: discovery_source
attributes.description: Method or channel through which the vulnerability was discovered (automated scan from Tenable/Qualys/Rapid7, penetration testing engagement, vendor security advisory, security research, incident response, manual audit).
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: exploitability_assessment
attributes.description: Assessment of the likelihood and ease of exploiting this vulnerability in the wild: active-exploit (known active exploitation), proof-of-concept (exploit code publicly available), theoretical (exploit possible but not demonstrated), unlikely (difficult to exploit).
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: false_positive_justification
attributes.description: Technical explanation for why the reported vulnerability is determined to be a false positive, including evidence and validation method. Required when remediation_status is false-positive.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-115 Technical Guide to Information Security Testing

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this vulnerability record, capturing status changes, remediation progress, or data corrections.

attributes.name: network_exposure
attributes.description: Network exposure classification of the affected asset: internet-facing (publicly accessible), internal (campus network only), isolated (air-gapped or restricted network), DMZ (demilitarized zone).
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-41 Guidelines on Firewalls and Firewall Policy

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, coordination notes, escalation history, or special handling instructions related to this vulnerability.

attributes.name: patch_identifier
attributes.description: Vendor-assigned identifier for the security patch or update that remediates this vulnerability (e.g., Microsoft KB number, Red Hat advisory ID).
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: remediation_action_taken
attributes.description: Description of the specific remediation action performed to address the vulnerability, such as patch applied, configuration changed, software upgraded, system decommissioned, or compensating control implemented.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: remediation_completed_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the vulnerability was successfully remediated through patching, configuration change, or other corrective action.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: remediation_due_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the vulnerability must be remediated, calculated based on institutional severity-based SLA policies (e.g., critical within 7 days, high within 30 days).
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: remediation_owner_department
attributes.description: Organizational department or unit responsible for remediation, such as IT Infrastructure, Application Development, or Network Services.

attributes.name: remediation_owner_name
attributes.description: Name of the individual or team responsible for remediating this vulnerability, typically the system owner, application owner, or infrastructure team lead.

attributes.name: remediation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the vulnerability remediation effort: open (newly discovered), in-remediation (work in progress), remediated (patched or fixed), accepted-risk (formally accepted by risk owner), false-positive (determined not to be a valid vulnerability), mitigated (compensating controls applied).
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: risk_acceptance_approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the risk acceptance decision was formally approved by the authorized risk owner.

attributes.name: risk_acceptance_approver_name
attributes.description: Name of the authorized individual (typically CISO, CIO, or senior IT leader) who formally approved the risk acceptance decision.

attributes.name: risk_acceptance_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the risk acceptance expires and must be re-evaluated or remediated, ensuring periodic review of accepted risks.

attributes.name: risk_acceptance_justification
attributes.description: Business and technical rationale for accepting the vulnerability risk without remediation, including compensating controls, business impact of remediation, and risk owner approval. Required when remediation_status is accepted-risk.

attributes.name: scan_identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the vulnerability scan or assessment run that detected this vulnerability, enabling traceability to the source scan report.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-115 Technical Guide to Information Security Testing

attributes.name: scanning_tool_name
attributes.description: Name of the automated vulnerability scanning tool that detected this vulnerability (e.g., Tenable Nessus, Qualys VMDR, Rapid7 InsightVM).
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-115 Technical Guide to Information Security Testing

attributes.name: severity_level
attributes.description: Categorical severity classification (critical, high, medium, low, informational) derived from CVSS base score and used to determine remediation SLA and prioritization.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: threat_intelligence_indicator
attributes.description: Reference to external threat intelligence sources or indicators of compromise (IOCs) associated with active exploitation of this vulnerability, used to elevate priority.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-150 Guide to Cyber Threat Information Sharing

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Concise descriptive title of the security vulnerability as reported by the scanning tool or security advisory.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: verification_scan_date
attributes.description: Date of the follow-up vulnerability scan performed to verify that the remediation action successfully eliminated the vulnerability.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: verification_status
attributes.description: Status of remediation verification: verified (confirmed resolved by rescan), pending-verification (awaiting rescan), failed-verification (still present after remediation attempt), not-applicable (verification not required for this remediation type).
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: vulnerability_description
attributes.description: Detailed technical description of the vulnerability, including the nature of the security weakness, potential exploit vectors, and impact to confidentiality, integrity, or availability.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-40 Guide to Enterprise Patch Management

attributes.name: related_vulnerability_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on vulnerability (related_vulnerability_id)

products.name: enterprise_application
products.description: Master record for every enterprise application in the institutional application portfolio, including ERP modules (Banner, Workday, PeopleSoft), SIS, LMS (Canvas), CRM, research administration systems, and departmental applications. Captures application name, application code, vendor, version, deployment model (on-premise, cloud SaaS, hybrid), hosting environment, primary business function, owning department, IT application owner, business application owner, data classification level (restricted, confidential, internal, public), integration dependencies, go-live date, contract expiration date, and lifecycle status (active, sunset-planned, decommissioned). Serves as the authoritative application portfolio registry for IT governance and enterprise architecture.

attributes.name: enterprise_application_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the enterprise application in the institutional application portfolio registry. Primary key for the enterprise application master record.

attributes.name: configuration_item_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.configuration_item. Business justification: Enterprise applications are configuration items in ITIL/CMDB frameworks. The configuration_item table's ci_class field would include 'application' as a CI type. This FK enables tracking applications a

attributes.name: accessibility_compliance_level
attributes.description: Level of web accessibility standards compliance for the application, ensuring usability for individuals with disabilities (WCAG for Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, Section 508 for US federal accessibility requirements).
attributes.references: WCAG 2.1, Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act, ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act)

attributes.name: api_availability
attributes.description: Type of programmatic API (Application Programming Interface) provided by the application for integration and data exchange with other systems.

attributes.name: application_category
attributes.description: High-level functional category classifying the application by its primary business domain (e.g., ERP for Enterprise Resource Planning, SIS for Student Information System, LMS for Learning Management System). attributes.name: application_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code or abbreviation used to uniquely identify the application in IT systems and documentation (e.g., BANNER, CANVAS, SLATE, WDAY).

attributes.name: application_name
attributes.description: Full business name of the enterprise application as known to users and stakeholders (e.g., Ellucian Banner Student Information System, Canvas Learning Management System).

attributes.name: authentication_method
attributes.description: Primary user authentication mechanism used by the application (SSO for Single Sign-On, SAML for Security Assertion Markup Language federation, LDAP for directory services, local credentials, OAuth, or multi-factor authentication).
attributes.references: Internal Identity and Access Management (IAM) Policy

attributes.name: backup_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which application data is backed up to support disaster recovery and data protection requirements.
attributes.references: Internal Data Backup and Recovery Policy

attributes.name: business_application_owner
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the business stakeholder or functional leader responsible for application strategy, requirements, and business outcomes.

attributes.name: compliance_frameworks
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of regulatory and compliance frameworks applicable to this application (e.g., FERPA, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, FISMA, GDPR, SOC 2) based on the data it processes and institutional requirements.
attributes.references: FERPA, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, FISMA, GDPR, Internal Compliance Policy

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this application record was first created in the enterprise application portfolio registry.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance and Audit Standards

attributes.name: criticality_rating
attributes.description: Business impact classification indicating the importance of the application to institutional operations (mission critical for essential services, high for important functions, medium for supporting services, low for convenience applications).

attributes.name: data_classification_level
attributes.description: Highest sensitivity level of data processed or stored by the application, determining security and access control requirements (restricted for FERPA/HIPAA data, confidential for business-sensitive, internal for operational, public for non-sensitive).
attributes.references: FERPA (Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act), Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: data_residency_location
attributes.description: Geographic location or jurisdiction where application data is physically stored, relevant for compliance with data sovereignty and privacy regulations.

attributes.name: deployment_model
attributes.description: Technical deployment architecture indicating where and how the application is hosted (on-premise data center, cloud Software-as-a-Service, hybrid model, or third-party hosted).

attributes.name: disaster_recovery_tier
attributes.description: Business continuity tier classification indicating recovery priority and RTO (Recovery Time Objective) requirements (Tier 1 for mission-critical with immediate recovery, Tier 2 for high priority, Tier 3 for moderate priority, Tier 4 for low priority).
attributes.references: Internal Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan

attributes.name: documentation_url
attributes.description: Web URL or repository location where application documentation, user guides, and technical specifications are maintained.

attributes.name: go_live_date
attributes.description: Date when the application was first deployed to production and made available to end users in the institutional environment.

attributes.name: hosting_environment
attributes.description: Specific hosting platform or infrastructure environment where the application runs (e.g., AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, on-campus data center, vendor cloud).
attributes.references: Internal Cloud Strategy and Infrastructure Standards

attributes.name: integration_dependencies
attributes.description: Comma-separated list or description of other enterprise applications or systems that this application integrates with via API (Application Programming Interface), ETL (Extract Transform Load), or other data exchange mechanisms.

attributes.name: is_mobile_enabled
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the application provides native mobile apps or mobile-responsive web interfaces for smartphone and tablet access.

attributes.name: is_sso_enabled
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the application is integrated with the institutional Single Sign-On (SSO) identity management system for seamless authentication.
attributes.references: Internal Identity and Access Management (IAM) Policy

attributes.name: it_application_owner
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the IT staff member responsible for technical administration, maintenance, and support of the application.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this application record was most recently updated in the enterprise application portfolio registry.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance and Audit Standards

attributes.name: last_security_assessment_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent security assessment, vulnerability scan, or penetration test conducted on the application.
attributes.references: Internal Information Security Policy, NIST Cybersecurity Framework

attributes.name: lifecycle_status
attributes.description: Current stage in the application lifecycle indicating operational status (active for production use, sunset planned for scheduled retirement, decommissioned for retired, under evaluation for assessment phase, implementation for deployment in progress, pilot for limited trial).

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the person who last modified this application record, supporting audit trail and data stewardship accountability.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance and Audit Standards

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional comments, special considerations, migration plans, known issues, or other contextual information about the application.

attributes.name: owning_department_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the institutional department or division that has primary business ownership and budgetary responsibility for the application.
attributes.references: Internal Organizational Hierarchy and Chart of Accounts

attributes.name: primary_business_function
attributes.description: Core business process or functional area that this application primarily supports (e.g., Student Registration, Financial Aid Administration, Course Content Delivery, Donor Management).
attributes.references: EDUCAUSE Core Data Service Functional Categories

attributes.name: product_version
attributes.description: Current version number or release identifier of the application software as deployed in the institutional environment.

attributes.name: replacement_application_code
attributes.description: Application code of the successor system that will replace this application if sunset is planned. Null if no replacement is identified.

attributes.name: sunset_date
attributes.description: Planned date for application retirement or decommissioning when lifecycle status is sunset planned. Null if no sunset is scheduled.

attributes.name: support_tier
attributes.description: Level of IT support coverage provided for the application (24x7 for round-the-clock support, business hours for standard coverage, best effort for limited support, vendor only for vendor-managed support).
attributes.references: Internal IT Service Management Framework, ITIL Standards

attributes.name: total_user_count
attributes.description: Total number of active user accounts or licenses provisioned for the application across all user populations (students, faculty, staff, external).

attributes.name: user_satisfaction_score
attributes.description: Average user satisfaction rating from surveys or feedback mechanisms, typically on a scale of 1.00 to 5.00, measuring end-user experience and application effectiveness.

attributes.name: vendor_name
attributes.description: Name of the software vendor or provider that develops and supports the application (e.g., Ellucian, Instructure, Workday, Oracle, Salesforce).
attributes.references: Internal Procurement and Vendor Management Policy

attributes.name: vendor_support_contact
attributes.description: Primary contact information (email or phone) for vendor technical support and escalation.

attributes.name: parent_enterprise_application_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on enterprise_application (parent_enterprise_application_id)

products.name: application_integration
products.description: Master record for every point-to-point or middleware-based integration between enterprise applications in the institutional integration landscape. Captures integration name, source application, target application, integration pattern (API, ETL batch, event-driven, file transfer), middleware platform (MuleSoft, Dell Boomi, Informatica, custom), data objects exchanged, integration frequency, data sensitivity classification, integration owner, operational status, last successful run timestamp, and error handling approach. Enables integration dependency mapping, impact analysis for application changes, and middleware governance.

attributes.name: application_integration_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the application integration record. Primary key.

attributes.name: primary_enterprise_application_id
attributes.description: Technical identifier or instance name of the source application system.

attributes.name: target_application_enterprise_application_id
attributes.description: Technical identifier or instance name of the target application system.

attributes.name: activation_date
attributes.description: Date when the integration was first activated and moved to production.

attributes.name: authentication_method
attributes.description: Authentication mechanism used to secure the integration connection (OAuth 2.0, SAML for federated identity, API Key, Basic Auth, Certificate-based, SSO for Single Sign-On, Kerberos for enterprise authentication).

attributes.name: average_record_volume
attributes.description: Average number of records or transactions processed per integration execution, used for capacity planning and performance monitoring.

attributes.name: business_criticality
attributes.description: Business impact classification of the integration (Critical for mission-critical processes with immediate business impact, High for important but not mission-critical, Medium for standard operational processes, Low for non-essential or convenience integrations).

attributes.name: compliance_requirements

attributes.name: identity_account_id
attributes.description: The user identifier of the person who created this contract record in the system. Used for audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: last_modified_by_user_identity_account_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Record Last Modified By User Identifier
attributes.description: The user identifier of the person who most recently modified this contract record. Used for audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: ledger_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.ledger_account. Business justification: IT contracts generate recurring expenses posted to specific GL accounts. Real business process: monthly contract expense accrual, budget vs actual variance analysis, financial statement preparation, n

attributes.name: owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the employee who is the designated business owner of this contract. This individual is responsible for contract performance monitoring, vendor relationship management, and renewal decisions.

attributes.name: primary_it_relationship_manager_employee_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Information Technology (IT) Relationship Manager Employee Identifier
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the IT staff member who serves as the primary relationship manager for this vendor contract. This individual coordinates technical requirements, service delivery, and escalations.

attributes.name: annual_cost
attributes.description: The annualized cost of the contract, representing the average yearly expenditure. For multi-year contracts, this is typically the total contract value divided by the number of years. For contracts with variable pricing, this represents the estimated or budgeted annual spend.
attributes.references: NACUBO Budgeting and Financial Planning Standards

attributes.name: auto_renewal_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the contract automatically renews for an additional term unless explicitly terminated or non-renewed by either party. True if auto-renewal clause is present, false otherwise.

attributes.name: business_associate_agreement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement is in place for this contract. Required when the vendor will have access to protected health information (PHI) from university health centers or medical schools. True if BAA is executed, false otherwise.
attributes.references: HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act)

attributes.name: contract_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the scope, deliverables, and purpose of the IT contract. Includes information about the systems, services, or infrastructure covered by the agreement.

attributes.name: contract_document_url
attributes.description: The URL or file path to the executed contract document stored in the institutional document management system or contract repository.

attributes.name: contract_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which the contract term expires. May be null for open-ended agreements or contracts with indefinite terms subject to termination clauses.

attributes.name: contract_number
attributes.description: The externally-known business identifier for the contract, typically assigned by procurement or vendor management systems. Used for reference in communications, invoices, and audit trails.

attributes.name: contract_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which the contract becomes effective and the vendor begins providing services or the institution begins incurring obligations under the agreement.

attributes.name: contract_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the IT contract. Indicates whether the contract is currently in force (active), awaiting renewal decision (pending_renewal), past its end date (expired), ended early (terminated), not yet executed (draft), or temporarily paused (suspended).

attributes.name: contract_type
attributes.description: Classification of the IT contract by service or product category. Distinguishes between hardware maintenance agreements, software subscriptions, professional services engagements, managed service agreements, and cloud service models (Infrastructure as a Service, Platform as a Service, Software as a Service). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: hardware_maintenance|software_subscription|professional_services|managed_service|cloud_iaas|cloud_paas|cloud_saas — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this contract record was first created in the IT contract management system. Used for audit trail and data lineage purposes.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code indicating the currency in which contract amounts are denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP, CAD).

attributes.name: data_privacy_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the contract includes data privacy and security provisions compliant with FERPA, HIPAA (if applicable), and other relevant data protection regulations. True if compliant provisions are present, false otherwise.
attributes.references: FERPA (Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act); HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act)

attributes.name: department_code
attributes.description: The organizational department code to which this contract is assigned for budgeting and cost allocation purposes. Typically represents the IT division or a specific IT functional area.

attributes.name: insurance_requirement_met_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the vendor has provided proof of required insurance coverage (general liability, professional liability, cyber liability, etc.) as specified in the contract terms. True if requirements are met and current, false otherwise.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this contract record was most recently updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking purposes.

attributes.name: last_renewal_date
attributes.description: The date on which the contract was most recently renewed or extended. Null for contracts that have never been renewed.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date for the next formal review of contract performance, pricing, and renewal decision. Typically set based on the renewal notice period to ensure timely action.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, comments, or special considerations related to the contract. May include information about unique terms, historical context, or operational considerations.

attributes.name: payment_frequency
attributes.description: The billing and payment cycle for the contract. Indicates how often the institution is invoiced and makes payments to the vendor.

attributes.name: purchase_order_number
attributes.description: The purchase order number issued by the procurement office to authorize expenditures under this contract. Links the IT contract to the institutional procurement and accounts payable systems.

attributes.name: renewal_notice_period_days
attributes.description: The number of days prior to contract expiration by which the institution must provide written notice if it intends to terminate or non-renew the contract. Critical for avoiding unintended auto-renewals.

attributes.name: service_level_agreement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the contract includes formal service level agreements with defined performance metrics, uptime guarantees, and remediation terms. True if SLA is present, false otherwise.

attributes.name: termination_for_convenience_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the contract includes a termination for convenience clause allowing the institution to end the agreement without cause, subject to notice requirements. True if such clause exists, false otherwise.

attributes.name: total_contract_value
attributes.description: The total financial value of the contract over its entire term, including all base fees, recurring charges, and committed expenditures. Excludes variable usage charges unless a minimum commitment is specified.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 87 - Leases; NACUBO Financial Reporting Standards

attributes.name: vendor_contact_email
attributes.description: The email address of the primary vendor contact for this contract. Used for operational communications and support requests.

attributes.name: vendor_contact_name
attributes.description: The name of the primary vendor representative or account manager for this contract. Used for operational communications and issue escalation.

attributes.name: vendor_contact_phone
attributes.description: The phone number of the primary vendor contact for this contract. Used for urgent communications and escalations.

attributes.name: renewed_it_contract_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on it_contract (renewed_it_contract_id)

products.name: it_risk
products.description: Master record for every identified technology risk in the institutional IT risk register, covering cybersecurity risks, operational risks, vendor risks, compliance risks, and disaster recovery risks. Captures risk identifier, risk title, risk category, risk description, affected systems or services, likelihood rating (1-5), impact rating (1-5), inherent risk score, control description, residual risk score, risk owner, risk treatment strategy (accept, mitigate, transfer, avoid), mitigation plan, target remediation date, and current risk status (open, mitigating, accepted, closed). Feeds institutional enterprise risk management (ERM) reporting and cybersecurity framework assessments (NIST CSF, ISO 27001).

attributes.name: it_risk_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the IT risk record in the institutional risk register.

attributes.name: affected_configuration_item_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.configuration_item. Business justification: IT risks should be linkable to the specific configuration items they threaten. The it_risk table currently has an 'affected_systems' string field, which is a denormalized list. Normalizing this to a F

attributes.name: affected_enterprise_application_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.enterprise_application. Business justification: IT risks should be linkable to the applications they affect. Application-specific risks (e.g., 'risk of ERP system data breach', 'risk of LMS vendor discontinuation') are common in enterprise IT risk

attributes.name: affected_it_service_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.it_service. Business justification: IT risks should be linkable to the services they threaten. Risk management in higher education IT focuses on service continuity (e.g., 'risk of email service disruption', 'risk of student portal unava

attributes.name: audit_finding_id
attributes.description: Identifier of a related internal or external audit finding that identified or contributed to this risk, supporting compliance and governance reporting.

attributes.name: incident_id
attributes.description: Identifier of a related cybersecurity incident, service disruption, or operational event that triggered or is associated with this risk, enabling traceability between risk management and incident response.

attributes.name: owner_employee_id
attributes.description: FK to hr.employee

attributes.name: primary_it_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the individual (typically a senior IT leader, department head, or business unit owner) who is accountable for managing, monitoring, and mitigating this risk.

attributes.name: actual_remediation_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the risk mitigation activities were completed and verified, used for tracking remediation performance and compliance.

attributes.name: business_continuity_impact_flag
attributes.description: Indicator of whether the risk, if realized, would disrupt critical institutional operations or services, affecting teaching, research, student services, or administrative functions.

attributes.name: compliance_framework
attributes.description: Regulatory, legal, or industry framework(s) to which this risk is relevant, such as FERPA (Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act), HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act), NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF), ISO 27001, PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard), or GLBA (Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act).
attributes.references: FERPA, HIPAA, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, GLBA

attributes.name: control_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of existing or planned controls, safeguards, countermeasures, or mitigation strategies implemented to reduce the likelihood or impact of the risk (e.g., multi-factor authentication (MFA), encryption, access controls, monitoring, training).

attributes.name: control_effectiveness
attributes.description: Assessment of how well the implemented controls are functioning to mitigate the risk: effective (controls are working as intended), partially effective (controls provide some mitigation but gaps remain), ineffective (controls are not reducing risk), or not implemented (controls are planned but not yet in place).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this risk record was first created in the IT risk register system, supporting audit trail and data lineage requirements.

attributes.name: data_breach_risk_flag
attributes.description: Indicator of whether the risk involves potential unauthorized access, disclosure, or loss of sensitive institutional data, including student records (FERPA), health information (HIPAA), payment card data (PCI DSS), or research data.
attributes.references: FERPA, HIPAA, PCI DSS, NIST SP 800-53

attributes.name: escalation_level
attributes.description: Level of organizational escalation required for this risk based on its severity and impact: operational (managed by IT operations), tactical (requires IT leadership attention), strategic (requires senior leadership or CIO attention), or executive (requires board or president attention).

attributes.name: financial_impact_estimate
attributes.description: Estimated financial cost or loss to the institution if the risk materializes, including direct costs (remediation, fines, legal fees) and indirect costs (reputational damage, lost revenue, operational disruption), expressed in US dollars (USD).

attributes.name: impact_rating
attributes.description: Assessment of the potential adverse effect on institutional operations, assets, or individuals if the risk materializes, rated on a scale of 1 (negligible) to 5 (catastrophic), considering financial, reputational, operational, and compliance dimensions.

attributes.name: inherent_risk_score
attributes.description: Calculated risk score before any controls or mitigations are applied, typically computed as likelihood_rating multiplied by impact_rating, representing the raw exposure level.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update or modification to this risk record, supporting change tracking and audit trail requirements.

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent review or reassessment of the risk, including updates to likelihood, impact, controls, and status.

attributes.name: likelihood_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative or quantitative assessment of the probability that the risk event will occur, rated on a scale of 1 (very unlikely) to 5 (very likely), based on threat intelligence, historical data, and environmental factors.

attributes.name: mitigation_plan
attributes.description: Detailed action plan outlining specific steps, resources, timelines, and responsibilities for implementing risk mitigation controls or remediation activities.

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the individual who last modified this risk record, supporting accountability and audit trail requirements.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next periodic review or reassessment of the risk, ensuring ongoing risk management and compliance with institutional policies.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional free-text notes, comments, or context related to the risk, including historical information, stakeholder feedback, or special considerations for risk management.

attributes.name: reputational_impact_flag
attributes.description: Indicator of whether the risk, if realized, would have significant reputational impact on the institution, affecting student enrollment, donor confidence, faculty recruitment, or public perception.

attributes.name: residual_risk_score
attributes.description: Calculated risk score after controls and mitigations have been applied, representing the remaining exposure level that the institution must accept or further mitigate.

attributes.name: risk_appetite_alignment
attributes.description: Assessment of whether the residual risk level aligns with the institutions defined risk appetite or tolerance: within appetite (acceptable level), exceeds appetite (requires additional mitigation or executive acceptance), or requires review (needs further analysis).

attributes.name: risk_category
attributes.description: Primary classification of the risk type: cybersecurity risks (threats to confidentiality, integrity, availability), operational risks (service disruptions, process failures), vendor risks (third-party dependencies), compliance risks (regulatory violations), disaster recovery risks (business continuity threats), or data privacy risks (FERPA, HIPAA violations).
attributes.references: NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF), ISO 27001, FERPA, HIPAA

attributes.name: risk_description
attributes.description: Comprehensive narrative description of the risk, including the threat source, vulnerability exploited, potential impact on institutional operations, and context for stakeholders.

attributes.name: risk_identification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the risk was first identified and documented in the institutional IT risk register.

attributes.name: risk_number
attributes.description: Business-facing unique identifier or reference number for the risk, used in risk register reports and communications with stakeholders.

attributes.name: risk_owner_department
attributes.description: Department or organizational unit to which the risk owner belongs, providing context for risk ownership and accountability.

attributes.name: risk_source
attributes.description: Origin or source of the risk identification, such as internal audit, vulnerability scan, penetration test, incident report, compliance assessment, vendor assessment, or strategic planning.

attributes.name: risk_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the risk: open (newly identified, awaiting action), mitigating (remediation activities in progress), accepted (risk acknowledged and accepted by leadership), closed (risk fully remediated or no longer applicable), or monitoring (risk under continuous observation).

attributes.name: risk_subcategory
attributes.description: Detailed subcategory or specific classification within the primary risk category, providing granular context for risk analysis and reporting.

attributes.name: risk_title
attributes.description: Concise title or name of the identified risk, summarizing the threat or vulnerability in business terms.

attributes.name: risk_treatment_strategy
attributes.description: Strategic approach selected for managing the risk: accept (acknowledge and monitor without further action), mitigate (implement controls to reduce likelihood or impact), transfer (shift risk to third party via insurance or contract), or avoid (eliminate the risk by discontinuing the activity or system).

attributes.name: target_remediation_date
attributes.description: Planned or target date by which the risk mitigation activities are expected to be completed and the residual risk reduced to an acceptable level.

attributes.name: third_party_vendor_name
attributes.description: Name of the third-party vendor, service provider, or partner associated with this risk, applicable for vendor risks, supply chain risks, or outsourced service risks.

attributes.name: parent_it_risk_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on it_risk (parent_it_risk_id)

products.name: it_sla_record
products.description: Transactional record capturing the measured SLA performance for each IT service against its defined targets for a given reporting period. Captures IT service reference, reporting period (month/quarter), SLA tier, availability target percentage, actual availability percentage, SLA met flag, mean time to resolve (MTTR) target in hours, actual MTTR in hours, total incidents in period, total service requests in period, customer satisfaction score average, and SLA breach count. Enables IT leadership to report service performance to institutional governance bodies and identify services requiring improvement investment.

attributes.name: it_sla_record_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Information Technology (IT) Service Level Agreement (SLA) Record Identifier (ID)
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the IT SLA performance record. Primary key for the IT SLA record entity.

attributes.name: it_service_id
attributes.description: Reference to the IT service for which SLA performance is being measured. Links to the IT service catalog entry.

attributes.name: primary_it_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee who is the designated service owner responsible for the overall performance and governance of this IT service.

attributes.name: actual_availability_percentage
attributes.description: The measured availability of the IT service during the reporting period, expressed as a percentage. Calculated as (total time - downtime) / total time * 100.

attributes.name: actual_first_contact_resolution_percentage
attributes.description: The actual measured percentage of incidents or service requests resolved on first contact during the reporting period.

attributes.name: actual_mttr_hours
attributes.business_glossary_term: Actual Mean Time to Resolve (MTTR) Hours
attributes.description: The actual measured mean time to resolve incidents for this IT service during the reporting period, measured in hours. Calculated as total resolution time divided by number of incidents.

attributes.name: actual_response_time_seconds
attributes.description: The actual measured average response time for the IT service during the reporting period, measured in seconds.

attributes.name: availability_target_percentage
attributes.description: The contractual or committed availability target for the IT service during the reporting period, expressed as a percentage (e.g., 99.95 for 99.95% uptime).

attributes.name: change_success_rate_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of changes to this IT service that were successfully implemented without causing incidents during the reporting period. Calculated as successful changes divided by total changes.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this SLA performance record was first created in the system. Follows format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: customer_satisfaction_score
attributes.description: The average customer satisfaction score for this IT service during the reporting period, typically measured on a scale of 1.00 to 5.00 based on user surveys.

attributes.name: first_contact_resolution_target_percentage
attributes.description: The target percentage of incidents or service requests resolved on first contact during the reporting period, without escalation or follow-up.

attributes.name: governance_review_date
attributes.description: The date this SLA performance record was reviewed by institutional IT governance bodies or leadership.

attributes.name: improvement_action_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the improvement actions or investments planned or required to address SLA performance gaps for this IT service.

attributes.name: improvement_action_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this IT service requires improvement investment or corrective action based on SLA performance. True if performance is below acceptable thresholds.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this SLA performance record was most recently updated or modified. Follows format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: major_incidents_count
attributes.description: The number of major incidents (high-impact, high-urgency incidents affecting multiple users or critical services) that occurred for this IT service during the reporting period.

attributes.name: mttr_target_hours
attributes.business_glossary_term: Mean Time to Resolve (MTTR) Target Hours
attributes.description: The target mean time to resolve incidents for this IT service during the reporting period, measured in hours. Represents the committed average resolution time.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, comments, or context regarding this SLA performance record, including explanations for breaches or exceptional circumstances.

attributes.name: planned_downtime_minutes
attributes.description: The number of minutes of planned or scheduled downtime for maintenance during the reporting period. Typically excluded from SLA availability calculations.

attributes.name: reporting_period_end_date
attributes.description: The last day of the reporting period for which SLA performance is measured (typically the last day of a month or quarter).

attributes.name: reporting_period_start_date
attributes.description: The first day of the reporting period for which SLA performance is measured (typically the first day of a month or quarter).

attributes.name: reporting_period_type
attributes.description: The granularity of the reporting period for SLA measurement (monthly, quarterly, annual, or weekly).

attributes.name: reporting_status
attributes.description: The current status of this SLA performance record in the reporting workflow (draft, submitted for review, approved by governance, or published to stakeholders).

attributes.name: response_time_target_seconds
attributes.description: The target average response time for the IT service during the reporting period, measured in seconds. Represents the committed time for the service to respond to user requests.

attributes.name: sla_breach_count
attributes.description: The total number of SLA breaches or violations that occurred for this IT service during the reporting period. Each breach represents a failure to meet a specific SLA target.

attributes.name: sla_met_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the IT service met all SLA targets for the reporting period. True if all targets were met, False if any target was breached.

attributes.name: sla_record_number
attributes.description: Business-facing unique identifier for this SLA performance record, used in reporting and governance communications.

attributes.name: sla_tier
attributes.description: The service tier or level of service commitment for this IT service (e.g., platinum for mission-critical services, bronze for best-effort services).

attributes.name: total_downtime_minutes
attributes.description: The total number of minutes the IT service was unavailable or down during the reporting period. Used to calculate actual availability percentage.

attributes.name: total_incidents_count
attributes.description: The total number of incidents logged against this IT service during the reporting period.

attributes.name: total_service_requests_count
attributes.description: The total number of service requests fulfilled for this IT service during the reporting period.

attributes.name: unplanned_downtime_minutes
attributes.description: The number of minutes of unplanned or unscheduled downtime due to incidents or failures during the reporting period. Counted against SLA availability targets.

attributes.name: prior_it_sla_record_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on it_sla_record (prior_it_sla_record_id)

products.name: it_chargeback
products.description: Transactional record of IT cost chargeback or cost allocation transactions issued to academic departments, administrative units, and research projects for consumption of centrally provided IT services. Captures billing period, charged department or cost center, IT service consumed, consumption quantity and unit of measure (GB storage, user seats, compute hours, print pages), unit rate, total charge amount, chargeback method (actual consumption, allocation formula, flat rate), invoice reference, and payment status. Supports IT financial transparency, departmental budget planning, and cost recovery for shared IT infrastructure.

attributes.name: it_chargeback_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the IT chargeback transaction record.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: The unique identifier of the IT financial manager or department head who approved this chargeback transaction for posting.

attributes.name: finance_fund_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.finance_fund. Business justification: IT cost recovery must align with fund accounting restrictions (general, auxiliary, restricted). Real business process: ensuring charges comply with fund purpose, auxiliary enterprise accounting, restr

attributes.name: grant_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.grant_account. Business justification: Sponsored research projects are charged for specialized IT services (HPC, secure storage, cloud). Real business process: grant expenditure tracking, F&A allocation, sponsor billing for direct IT costs

attributes.name: it_service_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.it_service. Business justification: IT chargebacks are issued for consumption of specific IT services. The it_service_code and it_service_name STRING fields should normalize to it_service_id FK. This links financial management to the se

attributes.name: ledger_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.ledger_account. Business justification: IT chargeback journal entries post to specific GL accounts for expense classification. Real business process: monthly IT cost allocation postings, financial statement preparation, natural account repo

attributes.name: principal_investigator_id
attributes.description: The unique identifier of the Principal Investigator responsible for the research project being charged. Applicable only when charges are allocated to sponsored research projects.

attributes.name: team_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to athletics.team. Business justification: Team-specific IT cost allocation for cloud storage (game film, recruiting video), video analysis software licenses, recruiting platform subscriptions, and support services. Financial reporting require

attributes.name: adjustment_amount
attributes.description: Any post-calculation adjustment to the chargeback amount due to billing corrections, dispute resolutions, or retroactive rate changes. May be positive or negative.

attributes.name: allocation_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of total IT service cost allocated to this department or project when using allocation formula chargeback method. Null for actual consumption or flat rate methods.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the chargeback transaction was approved for posting to departmental or project budgets.

attributes.name: billing_period_end_date
attributes.description: The last date of the billing period for which IT service consumption is being charged back.

attributes.name: billing_period_start_date
attributes.description: The first date of the billing period for which IT service consumption is being charged back.

attributes.name: chargeback_method
attributes.description: The methodology used to calculate and allocate IT costs to departments or projects. Actual consumption charges based on metered usage; allocation formula distributes shared costs using predefined ratios; flat rate applies fixed periodic charges; tiered rate varies by consumption volume; subscription charges fixed fee for defined service level.

attributes.name: chargeback_number
attributes.description: Human-readable business identifier for the chargeback transaction, typically formatted as CHG-YYYYMMDD or similar sequential numbering scheme.

attributes.name: charged_department_code
attributes.description: The organizational department code or cost center identifier to which the IT service charges are allocated. May represent academic departments, administrative units, or research projects.

attributes.name: charged_department_name
attributes.description: The full name of the department, administrative unit, or research project being charged for IT service consumption.

attributes.name: consumption_quantity
attributes.description: The measured quantity of IT service consumed during the billing period. Interpretation depends on the unit of measure (e.g., 500 GB, 100 user seats, 1000 compute hours).
attributes.references: Internal IT Metering and Usage Tracking

attributes.name: cost_center_code
attributes.description: The financial cost center code used for budget tracking and financial reporting in the institutional Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system.
attributes.references: Oracle PeopleSoft Financials Chart of Accounts

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this chargeback transaction record was first created in the IT financial system.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the charge amount. Typically USD for U.S. higher education institutions.

attributes.name: discount_amount
attributes.description: Any discount applied to the chargeback amount, such as volume discounts, promotional credits, or special program subsidies. Reduces the net amount charged.

attributes.name: dispute_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the charged department or project has disputed this chargeback transaction. True indicates an active or resolved dispute exists.

attributes.name: dispute_reason
attributes.description: The reason provided by the charged department for disputing the chargeback, such as incorrect usage measurement, wrong rate applied, or service not received. Null if no dispute exists.

attributes.name: dispute_resolution_date
attributes.description: The date when a disputed chargeback was resolved through investigation, adjustment, or mutual agreement. Null if no dispute or dispute is still open.

attributes.name: fiscal_period
attributes.description: The fiscal period or accounting month within the fiscal year (typically 01-12) to which this chargeback is posted.

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: The institutional fiscal year to which this chargeback transaction is attributed for budget and financial reporting purposes.

attributes.name: invoice_date
attributes.description: The date the invoice was generated and issued to the charged department or project.

attributes.name: invoice_number
attributes.description: The invoice reference number generated by the IT financial system or institutional billing system for this chargeback transaction.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this chargeback transaction record was most recently updated or modified.

attributes.name: net_charge_amount
attributes.description: The final net amount charged after applying discounts and adjustments. This is the amount posted to the departmental or project budget.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes providing additional context about the chargeback transaction, such as special circumstances, manual adjustments, or communication with the charged department.

attributes.name: payment_date
attributes.description: The date when payment or budget transfer was completed for this chargeback transaction. Null if payment is still pending.

attributes.name: payment_due_date
attributes.description: The date by which payment or budget transfer is expected to be completed for this chargeback transaction.

attributes.name: payment_reference_number
attributes.description: The reference number or transaction identifier from the financial system confirming the budget transfer or payment for this chargeback.

attributes.name: payment_status
attributes.description: The current payment status of the chargeback transaction, tracking whether the charged department or project has completed the budget transfer or payment.

attributes.name: project_code
attributes.description: The research project or grant identifier when IT services are charged to sponsored research activities. Null for non-research departmental charges.

attributes.name: service_category
attributes.description: The high-level category of IT service being charged, used for cost analysis and budget planning across service portfolios. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Infrastructure|Application|Security|Support|Communication|Storage|Compute|Network — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: total_charge_amount
attributes.description: The total dollar amount charged to the department or project for IT service consumption during the billing period. Typically calculated as consumption quantity multiplied by unit rate, with possible adjustments.

attributes.name: transaction_date
attributes.description: The date when the chargeback transaction was recorded and posted to the departmental or project account.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit in which IT service consumption is measured and billed, such as gigabytes for storage, user seats for software licenses, compute hours for virtual machines, or pages for printing services. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: GB|TB|User Seat|Compute Hour|CPU Hour|Transaction|Page|Device|License|Connection — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: unit_rate

products.name: application_contract_coverage
products.description: This association product represents the contractual coverage relationship between enterprise applications and IT vendor contracts. It captures which applications are covered under which contracts for cost allocation, license tracking, and renewal planning. Each record links one enterprise application to one IT contract with attributes that exist only in the context of this coverage relationship, including allocated costs, license quantities, coverage periods, and the role the contract plays for that specific application.. Existence Justification: In higher education IT portfolio management, enterprise applications are frequently covered by multiple vendor contracts simultaneously - for example, an ERP system may have separate contracts for the base software license, maintenance support, cloud hosting infrastructure, and professional services. Conversely, enterprise license agreements and cloud subscription contracts routinely cover multiple applications from the same vendor or technology stack. The business actively manages these coverage relationships for cost allocation, renewal planning, license compliance tracking, and vendor relationship management.
